elena: hey team, elena here — first-day build from source failing with undefined references to cuBLASLt and weird mixed-toolkit paths. any quick tips?

elena: build: `./build.sh --targets=runtime`
elena: linker snippet:
```
/usr/bin/ld: /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcublas.so: undefined reference to `cublasLtMatmul`
collect2: error: ld returned 1 exit status
```
mike: welcome! :wave: looks like linker is finding distro libcublas in /usr/lib while nvcc headers are from /usr/local/cuda-12.1. check `readlink -f /usr/local/cuda` and `echo $CUDA_HOME`.
devon: also run `ldconfig -p | grep cublas` and `which ptxas` — we've hit this when the system had an older packaging of cuda libs installed alongside a newer runfile. simplest fix: run `scripts/setup_cuda.sh` in repo, then clean cmake cache and rebuild.
elena: `readlink -f /usr/local/cuda` -> `/usr/local/cuda-12.1`; `ldconfig -p | grep cublas` shows entries in /usr/lib and /opt/cuda-12.2/lib64.
mike: aha — mixed installs. If you can, install the distro toolkit matching your headers (or update the /usr/local/cuda symlink to point to 12.2) and ensure PATH/LD_LIBRARY_PATH prefer the matching install. We also added a compatibility shim in `third_party/cublas_compat` but it's flaky for some ops.
elena: I switched `/usr/local/cuda` to the 12.2 runfile install and exported `CUDA_HOME=/usr/local/cuda`. cleaned build dir and retried — link now succeeds. thanks!
setup-bot: Hi elena! Please remember to finish the "Runtime dev setup" checklist and sign up for a mentor slot.
elena: will file a tiny PR to the README noting this mixed-install pitfall.
_description: New hire onboarding thread: linker errors from mixed CUDA installs; team recommends setup script, checking symlinks, cleaning cmake cache, and using matching toolkit (12.2)
